When client-side rendering is enabled in the Studio, allow the experimental Chromium HTML-in-canvas API to be used for capturing frames. See [HTML-in-canvas docs](/docs/client-side-rendering/html-in-canvas).

## CLI flag

Use `--allow-html-in-canvas` with the following commands. Follow a command link for its syntax and examples.

| Command                               | Flag                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| [`remotion studio`](/docs/cli/studio) | `--allow-html-in-canvas` |

## API and configuration references

Follow a reference for the parameter name, default value, and examples in that API or configuration method.

| Reference                                                                        | Name                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| [Configuration file](/docs/config#setallowhtmlincanvasenabled)                   | `Config.setAllowHtmlInCanvasEnabled()` |
| [`renderMediaOnWeb()`](/docs/web-renderer/render-media-on-web#allowhtmlincanvas) | `allowHtmlInCanvas`                    |
| [`renderStillOnWeb()`](/docs/web-renderer/render-still-on-web#allowhtmlincanvas) | `allowHtmlInCanvas`                    |
